(p-160) The second: He enriched you with the wealth of Khadijah, making you independent of Abu Talib; this was said by a group of exegetes.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]﴾. There are two opinions.

One: do not belittle him; this was said by Mujahid.

The second: do not oppress him regarding his wealth; this was said by al-Zajjaj. ﴿And as for the beggar﴾, there are two opinions.

One: the beggar seeking kindness; this was said by the majority. The meaning: when the beggar comes to you, either give to him or turn him away gently. The meaning of ﴿do not repulse﴾ is do not drive him away; one says "nahara" and "intahara" when one confronts someone with words that rebuke him.

The second: that he is a seeker of knowledge; this was said by Yahya ibn Adam and others.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And as for the favour of your Lord, proclaim [it]﴾. Regarding the favour there are three opinions.

One: prophethood.

The second: the Qur'an; both are related from Mujahid.

The third: that it is general, encompassing all goods; this is the view of Muqatil. It has been related from Mujahid that he said: "I recited to Ibn Abbas, and when I reached ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ he said: 'Glorify (takbir) when you finish each surah until you complete the Qur'an.' When ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said takbir in joy at the descent of revelation, and people made it a Sunnah.

Surah 93: Al-Duha

It is Meccan in its entirety, by the consensus of scholars.

The exegetes agree that this surah was revealed after a period in which revelation had ceased. Then they differed about the cause of that cessation, according to three opinions.

The first: "The Jews asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about Dhu al-Qarnayn, the People of the Cave, and the Spirit, and he said, 'I will inform you tomorrow,' without saying, 'If Allah wills.' So revelation was withheld from him."

The second: it was due to a lack of cleanliness among some of his companions. We have mentioned these two opinions in the commentary on Surah Maryam [19:65].

The third: it was on account of a puppy that was in his house. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

(p-155) As for the length of the period of its withholding, there are opinions which we have mentioned in the commentary on Surah Maryam [19:66].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihayn related from the hadith of Jundub, who said: "A woman from Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ), 'I see that your devil has forsaken you,' and so there was revealed: ﴿By the morning brightness﴾ ﴿and by the night when it is still﴾ ﴿Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor detested [you]﴾." Jundub is Ibn Sufyan. The woman is said to have been called Umm Jamil, the wife of Abu Lahab.

(p-156) Regarding the meaning of "ad-Duha" (the morning brightness) there are four opinions.

The first: the light of the day; this was said by Mujahid.

The second: the early part of the day; this was said by Qatadah.

The third: the first hour of the day when the sun has risen high; this was said by al-Suddi and Muqatil.

The fourth: the entire day; this was said by al-Farra'.

Regarding the meaning of "sajā" (is still) there are five opinions.

The first: it grew dark.

The second: it departed; this is related from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it came on; this was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The fourth: it became still; this was said by Ata', Ikrimah and Ibn Zayd. According to this, there are two views regarding the meaning of "became still":

One of them: its darkness settled. al-Farra' said: "sajā" means it grew dark and became motionless in its length, as one says "a sajī sea" and "a sajī night" when it is motionless and dark. "Motionless" means still. Abu Ubaydah said: one says "a night that is sājiyah, sākinah and shākirah." The reciter (al-Hadi) said:

Oh, how I love the moonlit night and the sājh (still) night,
And roads like the sheets of the weaver!

Ibn Qutaybah said: "sajā" means became still, and that is when its darkness has reached its end and it is motionless.

The second: the creatures became still in it; this was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

The fifth: its darkness extended; this was said by Ibn al-A'rabi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Anas, Urwah, Abu al-Aliyah, Ibn Ya'mar, Ibn Abi Ablah, and Abu Hatim from Ya'qub read "ma wadaʿaka" with a light dal. This is the answer to the oath. Abu Ubaydah said: "ma wadda'aka" is from taws'īd (bidding farewell), as one bids farewell to someone departing, and "ma wada'aka" with a light dal is from wada'ahu, yada'uhu. ﴿Nor has He detested [you]﴾, that is, He has not hated you.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾. Ata' said: better for you than the world. Others said: what awaits you in the Hereafter is greater than what He has given you of the honour of this world.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied﴾, of good in the Hereafter, ﴿so you will be satisfied﴾ with what you are given. Ali and al-Hasan said: it is intercession for his community until he is satisfied. Ibn Abbas said: (p-158) "What would be opened after him for his community, nation by nation, was shown to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was pleased by that, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first.﴾ ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied.﴾"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge?﴾ There are two opinions regarding this.

One: He made a refuge for you when He placed you under the care of your uncle Abu Talib, who relieved you of the burden; this was said by Muqatil.

The second: He made a refuge for you within yourself, which made you independent of Abu Talib's guardianship; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾. There are six opinions regarding this.

The first: lost from the landmarks of prophethood and the rulings of the Shariah, and He guided you to them; this was said by the majority, including al-Hasan and al-Dahhak.

The second: that he went astray as a small child in the valleys of Mecca, and Allah returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib; this was narrated by Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas.

(p-159) The third: "When he went out with Maysarah, the servant of Khadijah, Iblis took hold of the reins of his camel and turned him away from the road. Then Gabriel came, and Iblis blew a breath from which he fell to Abyssinia, and he returned him to the caravan; Allah bestowed this favour upon him." This was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

The fourth: the meaning is: He found you among a misguided people, and He guided you to monotheism and prophethood; this was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The fifth: He found you forgetful, and He guided you to remembrance. Similar to it is: ﴿that if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ [2:282]; this was said by Tha'lab.

The sixth: He found you unknown, unmentioned and unrecognised, and He guided people to you until they knew you; this was said by Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi.

And the poor man does not know when his wealth will come,
And the rich man does not know when he will become poor.
